Requirements: The department is seeking applicants with a strong academic background, a clear sense of purpose, and intellectual maturity. In addition to meeting the university requirements for graduate admission, applicants must submit the following: Official Transcripts from all colleges and universities attended, Statement of Purpose, Three letters of recommendation, Writing Sample (e.g., a term paper, thesis chapter, or professional paper on a topic related to the applicant's research interests. A minimum of 20 units is required for the minor. All courses must be taken for a letter grade. All students must have a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0 in the courses taken for the minor. Courses applied to the minor may not be taken on a pass/no pass basis. All minor coursework must be taken at USC.

To apply for the USC DPT program, you must complete the USC Graduate Application and the Physical Therapist Centralized Application Service (PTCAS) application. These applications are separate and require different materials and deadlines. Required Application Materials include: Official transcripts from all colleges and universities attended; Three letters of recommendation; GRE scores are NOT required for the 2024 application cycle; TOEFL or IELTS scores (for international applicants); Personal Statement; Observation Hours Verification (at least 150 hours of physical therapy observation, volunteer, or work experience, completed in at least two different settings, one of which must be inpatient and one outpatient. All hours must be verified.); USC Graduate Application.

Applicants must submit materials both to USC and to the department. The Graduate Record Examinations (GRE) general test is required. Additional required documents for graduate admission include a Statement of Purpose, Letters of Recommendation, and Transcripts. Official GRE scores must be submitted directly to USC from ETS, institution code 4852. International applicants must also satisfy English proficiency requirements.

Applications are accepted for fall admission only. All applicants must meet the general admission requirements of the USC Graduate School. In addition to these requirements, applicants must submit: a statement of purpose, a writing sample (15-25 pages), letters of recommendation (3), official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended, GRE General Test scores (optional).

Applicants must submit either the Common Application or Coalition Application, which includes essay prompts, along with the USC Writing Supplement. Required documents include official high school transcripts, a counselor recommendation, and a teacher recommendation. Standardized test scores (SAT/ACT) are optional for the 2024, 2025, and 2026 application cycles. Additional financial aid documents are required for those applying for financial assistance.

Applicants to the MA in Computational Linguistics program are expected to have a bachelor's degree in linguistics, computer science, or a related field. Students from other backgrounds will be considered if they have completed substantial coursework in linguistics or computer science, as well as a demonstrated interest in the field. Applicants must submit the following materials: Official transcripts from all universities attended, Statement of purpose, Three letters of recommendation, GRE General Test scores (optional), Resume or curriculum vitae, A writing sample (optional), International applicants must also submit TOEFL or IELTS scores. See the USC Graduate Admission website for additional information regarding minimum scores. Specific requirements: A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0. A strong academic record, particularly in linguistics, computer science, mathematics, or related fields. Background in basic programming and data structures is desirable. Background in formal linguistics (syntax, semantics, phonology) is desirable.

Applicants for the M.A. in Contemporary Latino and Latin American Studies are expected to have a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must submit the following:

Online application
Transcripts from all colleges and universities attended
A statement of purpose (1,000–1,500 words). The statement of purpose should explain how the applicant’s academic and professional experiences have prepared them for graduate study in Contemporary Latino and Latin American Studies, and how this program will help them achieve their future goals.
Three letters of recommendation from faculty members or others qualified to evaluate the applicant’s academic and professional potential.
A writing sample (20–25 pages). The writing sample should be an academic paper, preferably one that focuses on topics related to the CLALS program.
GRE General Test scores are not required.
A current résumé or curriculum vitae (CV).

International applicants must submit a score of 90 on the TOEFL or 6.5 on the IELTS. For a list of eligible exemptions, please see the USC Graduate Admissions website: gradadm.usc.edu.
Program name: Contemporary Latino and Latin American Studies

Applicants for the MS and PhD degrees are expected to have a bachelor’s degree in geological sciences or a related field (e.g., biology, chemistry, computer science, engineering, environmental sciences, mathematics, or physics). Online Application, Application Fee, Transcripts, GRE General Test: Not Required, Resume/CV: Required, Statement of Purpose: Required, Letters of Recommendation: Required (3 letters), Writing Sample: Not Required, Portfolio: Optional, English Proficiency: Required for international students (TOEFL, IELTS, PTE).

Admission to the USC Rossier School of Education is a highly selective process. The admissions committee considers many factors in evaluating candidates, including academic record, test scores, letters of recommendation, statement of purpose, and professional experience. All applicants are required to possess a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must also meet the minimum requirements for admission to the USC Graduate School. Required documents include: Application for Admission, Statement of Purpose, Letters of Recommendation, Transcripts, GRE (Graduate Record Examinations) Scores, English Proficiency (for international students), California Basic Educational Skills Test (CBEST), California Subject Examinations for Teachers (CSET), U.S. Citizenship (if applicable).

Applicants must also submit a statement of purpose and three letters of recommendation. GRE scores are not required for admission to the Human Security and Geospatial Intelligence program. In addition to the requirements of the Graduate School, applicants must submit: The GRE General Test is required. Students who have a graduate degree from a U.S. institution or who are currently enrolled in a PhD program at USC are exempt from the GRE requirement. An average GRE score for admitted students is 155 verbal, 160 quantitative and 3.5 analytical writing. Only scores submitted electronically from ETS will be accepted. USC’s ETS institution code is 4852. Three letters of recommendation are required from faculty or supervisors. A resume is required. A statement of purpose is required. Official transcripts from all universities attended. Applicants whose native language is not English must submit scores for either the TOEFL or IELTS.
